sections.title: Integration Workflow
sections.text:
15.1 Integration Workflow
The stability study with a material requires a decent knowledge of four different SAP
S/4HANA areas: quality management (QM), production planning (PP), plant mainte-
nance (PM), and materials management (MM). It’s in the QM area that the stability

15 Stability Study
650
study with (or without) a material is performed, along with several associated activi-
ties, such as results recording and usage decision.
In the actual business process of conducting a stability study, all the related depart-
ments of the company come together to contribute to their share of this endeavor (sta-
bility study). This includes, but isn’t limited to, the decision-making process to
determine which of the following options you’ll choose:
 Proceed with the full-fledged stability study, or cancel it after the initial test
 Revise the testing schedule of storage conditions, or shorten or prolong it
 Cancel the stability study, or simply “deactivate” it for a limited time to be reacti-
vated later
Figure 15.1 provides a better picture of the stability study workflow.
Figure 15.1 Stability Study Workflow
The stability study with (or without) a material draws its fundamental concept from the
notification in QM. In fact, the first step toward creating a stability study begins with cre-
ating a special QM notification that’s available for stability studies only. Hence, this chap-
ter will intermittently refer to stability studies with either a material or a notification.

15.2 Master Data
For the stability study, inspection types 16, 1601, and 1602 are applicable. Table 15.1
explains each of the three inspection types in the material master and their roles in the
stability study. We’ll cover the actual applications of all three inspection types in this
chapter.
Note
The inspection plans’ usage for all three inspection types is 9 (Material Check).
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
We’ll now cover every step of the stability study with a material. We’ll also address all
the options and choices available in the Action Box of the stability study with a mate-
rial. To facilitate the understanding and learning process, we’ll move in a logical order
so that it’s easier to comprehend the relationship between each sequential action
during the stability study for a material.

sections.title: Create Stability Study with a Material
sections.text:
15.3.1 Create Stability Study with a Material
To create a new stability study with a material, use Transaction QST01 or follow menu
path Logistics  Quality Management  Stability Study  Stability Study  Create. On the
initial screen for creating a stability study, enter the notification type QS, which is for
stability study with a material, and an internal notification/stability study number that
the system generates, which in this example is 800000004. Then, press (Enter) to go
to the screen in Figure 15.2. As previously explained, a stability study is a special form of
quality notification. Further, the notification type QS is available in the standard SAP
model company provided by SAP.
Note
If you need to work with a stability study without a material, then the available notifi-
cation type in the IDES system is QR. In a stability study without a material, there is no
reference to a material or its associated batch number. However, all the steps that we
cover in this chapter for a stability study with a material are equally applicable to a sta-
bility study without a material (but without direct reference to a material or batch
number).
The system also offers another notification type, QT, which is for a stability study trial.
This stability study type uses predefined and preconfigured building blocks consisting
of planning data to facilitate the stability study.
In Figure 15.2, enter Material “2234” and Plant “1710”. Because this material is batch-
managed, the system requires the batch number, along with the storage location. We
assign these as 121 and 171A, respectively. Prior to starting the stability study with a
material, you can create a batch for this material and plant with Transaction MSC1N. If
you’ve maintained the date of manufacturing and expiration date (shelf-life expiration
date/best-before date [SLED/BBD]) of the batch, then these will also automatically
appear in the stability study screen. The entire chapter will refer to not just this mate-
rial but also its corresponding batch number, 121, available at storage location 171A.
Note
The focus of this entire chapter is on the tasks shown in the Action Box on the right
side of Figure 15.2. We’ll cover each of these tasks in detail. We’ll cover the first two
steps of the Action Box, Display Objects for Study and Display Stability History, at the
end of the chapter. This approach will make sense when we’ve performed necessary
actions for the stability study and the relevant information becomes available in the
first two objects of the Action Box.
Let’s start with step number three of the Action Box, which is Create Initial Sample, and
then proceed with each step of the Action Box in sequential order.
© 

653
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.2 Detailed Screen of Stability Study with Material and Action Box
Note
We’ll refer to Figure 15.2 and/or the Action Box in the rest of this chapter, unless other-
wise mentioned.

sections.title: Initial Sample
sections.text:
15.3.2 Initial Sample
Before an actual stability study begins, it’s important to create an initial sample of the
stability study. The initial sample is the physical sample of the stability study. This
physical sample goes through the regular QM tasks of results recording, defects record-
ing (if any), and usage decision to validate the process and decide whether a full-fledged
stability study should continue or not. Just as with normal inspection, the initial sam-
ple for the stability study also contains comprehensive details related to sample size,
packing, sample location, and storage condition.
In the following sections, we’ll show how to create, change, and then confirm an initial
sample. An initial sample needs to be confirmed to proceed further with the stability
study.

15 Stability Study
654
Create
Choose Create Initial Sample from Action Box to go to Figure 15.3. Here, enter the details
that relate to sample container, sample quantity, storage condition, and sample loca-
tion. Choose Save and Change Notification. On saving, the system creates a physical
sample, which in this example is 900000026. Because this is the initial sample, this ref-
erence of the initial sample remains available throughout the entire process of the cov-
ering stability study with material.
Figure 15.3 Creating Initial Sample
Change
If you need to make any changes after creating an initial sample, then choose Change
Initial Sample from Action Box, as shown in Figure 15.4. Notice that in change mode, the
system has already created a physical sample 900000026 with the status set as created
(CRTD). Make any desired changes, such as changing the sample size from a quantity of
3 (as first defined in Figure 15.3) to 2 PC. Choose Save and Change Notification in Figure
15.4. Doing so saves the changes you’ve made and brings you back to the change notifi-
cation (stability study) screen.
© 

655
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.4 Changing Initial Sample
Confirm
The next step is the confirmation of the initial sample. A confirmation validates that
the initial sample can form the basis of proceeding further with the stability study. To
confirm an initial sample, choose Confirm Initial Sample in Action Box to go to Figure
15.5. This screen contains the previously entered information of the initial sample.
Notice the option to enter the No. (number) of Labels for the initial sample. You can
print these labels and physically paste them onto the physical samples’ containers.
Enter the number of labels to be printed as “3”, and choose Save and Change Notifica-
tion to go to the screen shown in Figure 15.6, which is a popup that appears with the pro-
vision to add or update additional information and relates to the confirmation of the
initial sample. Enter or update the information, and choose Continue. The system
accordingly updates the status of the physical sample of the initial test to REL (released).

15 Stability Study
656
Figure 15.5 Confirmation of Initial Sample
Figure 15.6 Additional Details for Confirmation of Initial Sample

sections.title: Bill of Materials
sections.text:
15.3.3 Bill of Materials
Because we’re creating the stability study with a material, the system allows you to
enter details of the components used in the stability study. These components are in
the form of a bill of materials (BOM). A BOM contains the details of an individual com-
ponent, together with its quantity.
The following sections will discuss how to assign a BOM to a stability study and be able
to maintain it subsequently.
© 

657
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Assign
Choose Assign Bill of Material in Action Box to go to Figure 15.7.
Figure 15.7 Assign Bill of Materials
Here, the system also allows entering a BOM of another material. Notice that the Usage
of the BOM in Figure 15.7 is defined as a stability study. This usage prevents the BOM
from being used in the normal production process. The stability study usage of a BOM
has limited functions because material is still going through the development, trial,
and testing phases. When the stability study is successful, you can change the BOM
usage to 1, which is for production. Choose Assign Bill of Material.
Tips and Tricks
We suggest creating a BOM for the material and its usage 8 beforehand so that you
can assign it in this step. To create a material BOM, use Transaction CS01. This is an
integration point between QM and PP.
Further, to ensure that Usage 8 is allowed in Figure 15.7, make the necessary entry in
Transaction OS21 if it doesn’t exist.
Maintain
After the initial assignment of a material BOM to the stability study, you can also make
further changes to it if needed. These changes can include, for example, the deletion of
a BOM component or a change in the quantity.
To make changes in the BOM, choose Maintain Bill of Material in Action Box to go to the
change screen for the BOM shown in Figure 15.8. Notice that one of the components is

15 Stability Study
658
RM20, with a quantity of 10 PC (pieces). If needed, you can change the quantity of this
component or even add a new component. Choose Save to save the BOM.
Figure 15.8 Changes to Bill of Materials

sections.title: Initial Test Inspection Lot: Inspection Type 1601
sections.text:
15.3.4 Initial Test Inspection Lot: Inspection Type 1601
After the confirmation of the initial sample, the next important step is the creation of
an inspection lot for the initial test in the stability study. An inspection lot for the ini-
tial test automatically creates an inspection lot of inspection type 1601.
Warning
Until the initial sample is confirmed, you can’t create an inspection lot for the initial
test of the stability study. The system checks that the physical sample has the released
(REL) status, and if so, allows inspection lot creation. This shows the importance of fol-
lowing the sequence of steps given in Action Box.
In Action Box, choose Initial Test Inspection Lot to go to the screen in Figure 15.9. Notice
that the physical sample 900000026 is the same physical sample that we’ve worked on
in the previous steps. The inspection lot, which the system creates, is inspection type
1601. You can manually assign the task list Group “7” and Group Counter “1”, which we
previously covered in Section 15.2, as part of the stability study master data.
Choose Inspection Lot in Figure 15.9 to create an inspection lot and to go to the screen
in Figure 15.10.
Figure 15.10 shows the selection screen for master inspection characteristics that the
system brings up for inspection lot results recording and usage decision. The master
inspection characteristics are taken from the inspection plan that was previously avail-
able as a part of the QM master data.
© 

659
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.9 Creating Inspection Lot for Initial Test Inspection
Figure 15.10 Option to Flexibly Select or Change Details of Master Inspection Characteristics
Notice the flexibility you have in selecting the relevant master inspection characteris-
tics, which are then available for results recording and usage decision. At this stage, you
can also change the other details, such as lower or upper limits or even the target value
of any master inspection characteristic. For this example, first choose Select All to
select all the master inspection characteristics, and then choose Copy All to copy all the
master inspection characteristics to the inspection lot.
With this step, the system creates a new inspection lot for the initial test of the stability
study with inspection type 1601. For this example, this inspection lot number is
160000000005.

15 Stability Study
660
Now that the system has created an inspection lot for the initial conditions for the sta-
bility study, we’ll briefly discuss the associated QM activities, such as results recording
and usage decisions, before we return to Action Box to cover the remaining available
options.

sections.title: Inspection Process for an Initial Sample: Results Recording and Usage
sections.text:
15.3.5 Inspection Process for an Initial Sample: Results Recording and Usage
Decision
Because the results recording and usage decisions are standard QM activities, we’ll
quickly walk you through how the system incorporates all the information and details
from the stability study into the newly created inspection lot, as well as the role of
inspection points. To record results, use Transaction QE01, and on the initial screen,
enter Inspection Lot “160000000005” and Operation “0010”. Press (Enter), and the
system shows the Assigned Insp. Pnt button. Click once, and the system automatically
assigns physical sample 900000026.
Figure 15.11 appears after we’ve entered the results of operation 0010, and it also con-
tains details of physical sample 900000026 against the inspection lot. Save the entries
and repeat the same steps for operation 0010 so that the screen in Figure 15.12 appears.
This step highlights the importance of the inspection points that we previously covered.
Figure 15.11 Initial Screen for Results Recording of Inspection Lot
Choose the Samples Overview for Material button located at the bottom-right side of
the screen shown in Figure 15.13, which shows not just the initial phyicsal sample
900000026 associated with this inspection lot but also other additional details.
© 

661
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.12 Results Recording of Inspection Lot
Figure 15.13 Usage Decision of Inspection Lot
For the usage decision, use Transaction QA11, and on the initial screen, enter Inspection
Lot “160000000005”. In the screen in Figure 15.13, enter the usage decision code (UD
Code) as “0010” and “STABI” to accept and approve the results of the initial test inspec-
tion for the stability study. This usage decision code selection also confirms that we’ll
proceed with executing the stability study. Choose the Samples tab to go to the screen
in Figure 15.14.

15 Stability Study
662
Figure 15.14 Detailed Screen for Physical Samples of Inspection Lot
Figure 15.14 shows the detail screen for physical sample 900000026 and its corre-
sponding operation used in the initial test inspection lot for the stability study. Save
your entries. You then receive a message confirming the successful completion of the
initial test for notification type 800000004.
So far, we’ve created, confirmed, and approved the initial test inspection lot for the sta-
bility study by means of results recording and usage decision. Let’s return to the
remaining steps and options available in Action Box for a stability study with a mate-
rial.

sections.title: Change Notification
sections.text:
15.3.6 Change Notification
On saving the original notification 800000004 and performing other activities such
as results recording or usage decision, you can use the change notification option to
return to the stability study with a material.
To change the notification, use Transaction QM02 or menu path Logistics  Quality
Management  Stability Study  Stability Study  Change. On the initial screen for chang-
ing the notification type, enter the Notification “800000004”, and press (Enter). This
brings us back to the screen in Figure 15.2, but this time in change mode.

sections.title: Complete Initial Test
sections.text:
15.3.7 Complete Initial Test
In Action Box, choose Complete Initial Test. This confirms and saves the results of the
initial test of the inspection lot.
© 

663
15.3 Stability Study for a Material

sections.title: Storage Conditions
sections.text:
15.3.8 Storage Conditions
Because the inspection lot for the initial test was successful as well as approved, the
next step is to specify the storage condition(s) to keep the physical samples in. In Action
Box, choose Specify Storage Conditions. In the screen in Figure 15.15, enter the sample
quantity for each storage condition.
Figure 15.15 Define Storage Conditions of Stability Samples
In this example, enter a sample quantity of 1 PC; each is stored in Stor.Cond. (the first
column to the left) 00000001 with the text “Room Temperature 21°”, and in Stor.Cond.
00000002 with the text “Temperature 20°”. In addition, notice that the physical sam-
ple 900000026 now has the REL (for released) status. Select both Stor.Cond. 00000001
and Stor.Cond. 00000002, and choose Save and Change Notification.
Note
Storage conditions are covered in Section 15.4.3. You must carefully evaluate all the
storage conditions that you’ll need for the stability study, and ensure their availability
accordingly.

15 Stability Study
664
The following sections discuss the storage conditions and storage locations associated
with a stability study.
Specify Additional Storage Condition
You can define additional storage conditions if there is any such need during the stabil-
ity study. Choose Specify Add. Storage Conds in Action Box to arrive at the screen in
Figure 15.16.
Figure 15.16 Defining Additional Storage Conditions
Here, you have the option to incorporate an additional storage condition for your sam-
ples for the stability study. When you’ve made the necessary changes, choose Save and
Change Notification. In this example, we enter the sample location shown in Figure
15.16.
Store Stability Samples
To formally begin the stability study process, you need to store the physical samples in
the specified storage conditions. On doing so, the system updates the status of physical
© 

665
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
samples to REL (released). With this status of physical samples, the system enables
inspection lot creation, as well as all other standard QM activities, such as results
recording, defects recording, and usage decision. To place the stability sample in stor-
age, and according to chosen storage conditions, choose Store Stability Samples in
Action Box to go to Figure 15.17.
Figure 15.17 Store Stability Samples in Storage Conditions
Here, you update the storage date and sample location, along with the number of labels
required for printing. Choose the line item of storage condition 00000001, and then
choose Save and Change Notification. Notice that the physical sample at storage condi-
tion 00000001 still has the status CRTD. As soon as you save, the system updates the
status to REL to release the physical sample. For this example, the physical sample
number is 900000027 (the first field shown at the top in Figure 15.16).
Use Transaction QPR3 to display physical sample 900000027 and to confirm whether
the system updated the information on the physical sample accordingly (see Figure
15.18). Here, the system updates the physical sample’s status to REL and automatically
creates inspection lot 160000000007.
Because two physical samples were placed in two different storage conditions, the sec-
ond physical sample that the system automatically created is 900000028 and the
associated inspection lot.

15 Stability Study
666
Figure 15.18 Inspection Lot with Inspection Type 1602
Delete Storage Conditions
You can delete a storage condition when you no longer want to continue with a sample
placed in a certain storage condition. Choose Delete Storage Conditions in Action Box
to go to the screen shown in Figure 15.19. You can, for example, select storage condition
00000002 and choose Delete and Change Notification. Doing so will remove the sam-
ple from the stability study.
© 

667
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.19 Delete Storage Condition

sections.title: Testing Schedule
sections.text:
15.3.9 Testing Schedule
If the initial test for the stability study proves satisfactory, then the next step is to cre-
ate a testing schedule to monitor the progress or the physical and chemical conditions
of the stored samples in the storage conditions over a longer period of time. Setting up
a testing schedule enables the system to automatically create inspection lots per the
defined schedule to ensure the stability study’s timely results recording and usage
decisions.
The following sections discuss how to create and change a testing schedule of a stability
study and how to complete the testing schedule once the stability study is either com-
pleted or isn’t required anymore.
Create
In Action Box, choose Create Testing Schedule. In Figure 15.20, due to the number range
settings, the system internally assigns the Maintenance Plan 700020000002, whereas
the maintenance planning category (Maint. plan cat.) ST denotes that it’s applicable to
the stability study. A maintenance plan holds and controls all the information related

15 Stability Study
668
to planning and scheduling activities, including automatic creation of inspection lots,
on the due dates of inspections.
Figure 15.20 Testing Schedule of Inspection for Storage Conditions
The maintenance strategy QSTABI is assigned to maintenance plan 700020000002 and
is configured to create a new inspection lot every month for the material undergoing
the stability study. The Scheduling Period of 1 year (YR) denotes that the stability study
will last for one year; the system will create the number of inspection lots accordingly.
Finally, in this case, the system creates a monthly inspection lot of inspection type 16,
which is the inspection for storage condition. This inspection type compares with
inspection type 1601, which was specific to initial sample creation.
Note
The maintenance plan category is an object that we’ll cover in Section 15.4.7. In addition,
because maintenance strategies have extensive use in the PM area of SAP S/4HANA,
consider engaging a PM resource to set up the correct maintenance strategy for your
stability study. This is an integration point between QM and PM in the stability study.
Setting up a maintenance strategy is a business process and not a configuration step,
but we’ll cover it in Section 15.4.8 to maintain the ongoing business processes flow and
continuity of the stability study in this section.
Change
You can change the testing schedule of the stability study. This can be helpful when
there’s a need to change the testing frequency of the physical samples. You can also use
this option to enter any missing or incomplete information in the maintenance plan.
© 

669
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Choose Change Testing Schedule in Action Box. A popup appears, asking you to con-
firm whether you’d like to make changes to the testing schedule. Choose Yes so that the
system navigates to the screen in Figure 15.21.
Figure 15.21 Maintenance Plan for Changes in Testing Schedule
In Figure 15.21, update Group “7” and TL Group Counter “1” in the Inspection Plan area. If
you receive an error when doing so, follow these two troubleshooting steps:
1. Use Transaction CWBQM (Engineering Workbench), and in the popup that appears,
enter “Q_OPR_000000000010”, which will bring up operations details of the
inspection plan. On the screen that appears, enter Material “2234”, Plant “1710”, Task
List Type “Q”, Group “7”, and Group Counter “1”, and then choose Load Task Lists from
the top menu bar. In the Headers General tab of the screen that appears (see Figure
15.22), assign the maintenance Strategy as “QSTABI”. You’ll have to scroll to the far
right of the screen to find this field for assignment.

15 Stability Study
670
2. Select the first operation shown in Figure 15.22, and choose Task Lists  Maintenance
Packages, and maintain the monthly packages that belong to Strategy QSTABI, as
shown in Figure 15.23.
Figure 15.22 Assigning the Maintenance Strategy to the Inspection Plan
Figure 15.23 Assigning the Maintenance Package
Both these settings in the inspection plan for material 2234 and plant 1710 correspond
to the options selected in Figure 15.20 previously. Further, when you’ve made both set-
tings in the inspection plan via Transaction CWBQM (the Engineering Workbench) and
© 

671
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
not via the normal inspection plan’s Transaction QP02, where these options aren’t
available, you’ll be able to assign group 7 and group counter 1 to the maintenance plan,
as shown in Figure 15.22.
Tips and Tricks
You can also use Transaction IP02 to directly make changes to the maintenance plan
(testing schedule). Enter the maintenance plan 700020000002 on the initial screen
and press (Enter), and it takes you to Figure 15.21.
Furthermore, you can use Transaction IP10 to schedule automatic inspection lot cre-
ation, which is relevant for stability studies. On the initial screen of Transaction IP10,
enter the relevant maintenance planning category and maintenance strategy.
Complete
When the testing schedule for the stability study is complete, proceed to update the
same so that the system no longer automatically creates inspection lots. Alternatively,
you can complete the testing schedule anytime, as deemed necessary.
Choose Complete Test Scheduling in Action Box, and a popup appears, asking you to
confirm whether you’d like to set the status to Testing Scheduling Completed and
return to the stability study. Choose Yes.

sections.title: Inspection Lot for Inspection Type 16
sections.text:
15.3.10 Inspection Lot for Inspection Type 16
With the testing schedule now in place, the system automatically creates inspection
lot(s) of inspection type 16 on due date(s).
Warning
The status of the physical sample is still CRTD (created). Unless the physical sample
attains status REL (released), the system doesn’t create inspection lots. To set the phys-
ical samples’ status under storage conditions to REL, refer to Section 15.3.2.
Figure 15.24 shows the detailed screen of Inspection Lot 160000000006. Notice that
this screen has Inspection Type 16, notification 800000004, maintenance plan
700020000002 (not shown but located further down the same screen), and the strat-
egy for stability study STABI.
The rest of the steps are all the same as in standard QM activities, such as results record-
ing and usage decision, and we won’t repeat them here.

15 Stability Study
672
Figure 15.24 Automatic Creation of Inspection Lot by Testing Schedule
To check and test whether the system will create the inspection lot per the testing
schedule, follow these steps:
1. Store stability samples, as covered in Section 15.3.7, so that the physical samples
attain REL status. The system creates inspection lots only for physical samples with
the REL status.
2. Use Transaction IP10, and then on the initial screen, enter the maintenance plan. In
this example, it’s “700020000002”.
3. On the next screen, choose the Manual Call button to prompt the system to manu-
ally trigger inspection lot(s) creation. When the system asks for the date (in a Manual
Call field in a popup), enter today’s date, as shown in Figure 15.25.
4. Choose the Scheduled calls tab in Figure 15.26 to see the monthly scheduled mainte-
nance calls made.
5. Save your entries and check for the newly created inspection lot using Transaction
QA32 for inspection type 16 to bring up the screen in Figure 15.24, shown earlier.
© 

673
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.25 Start Date of Maintenance Cycle
Figure 15.26 Maintenance Plan 700020000002

sections.title: Print Labels
sections.text:
15.3.11 Print Labels
You can print the labels of storage conditions with details and paste them on physical
samples for quick and easy identification. To print labels, choose Print Labels in Action
Box. In Figure 15.27, enter the number of labels you’d like to print for samples in storage
conditions. For this example, enter “1” in the first column, select the line item, and
choose Print and Change Notification.

15 Stability Study
674
Figure 15.27 Print Labels for Storage Conditions
To send the print labels request to the printer spool, use Transaction SP02 or menu
path System  Own Spool Requests (see Figure 15.28). Here, you see the list of spool
requests for print jobs. Choose the Print Preview icon of spool number 13700, and the
screen in Figure 15.29 appears.
Figure 15.28 List of Spool Requests
© 

675
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.29 Labels Printing
Note
Consider engaging an ABAP consultant (programmer) to develop the layout/format of
the physical sample’s label that meets your company’s business needs.

sections.title: Define the Start Date of the Study
sections.text:
15.3.12 Define the Start Date of the Study
The start date of the stability study is the formal start of the stability study and the date
for the system to automatically create all further testing schedules. In Action Box,
choose Define Start Date of Study, and enter the start date for your stability study.
Choose Save and Change Notification.

sections.title: Manual Inspection Lot for Storage Condition: Inspection Type 1602
sections.text:
15.3.13 Manual Inspection Lot for Storage Condition: Inspection Type 1602
At any point in time, you can also create a manual inspection lot for the storage condi-
tion of physical samples of your stability study. The inspection type for manually cre-
ated inspection lots is 1602.
In Action Box, choose Manual Insp. Lot f. Stor. Cond., and the screen in Figure 15.30
appears. Here, you see that the system already has Inspection Lot 160000000006
placed under Stor.Cond. 00000001. This inspection lot is the same one that the system
created through testing the schedule.
Select the line item containing Inspection Lot 160000000006, placed under Stor.Cond.
00000001, and choose Create Manual Inspection Lot And Change Notification. When
you do so, the screen in Figure 15.31 appears, in which the system automatically sug-
gests inspection type 1602. For this example, however, enter “7” for Group and “1” for
Group Counter, as well as short text, and choose Inspection Lot. This step brings up the
screen in Figure 15.32 to help you select the master inspection characteristics. The rest
of the steps are all the same that we’ve previously covered in this chapter, so we won’t
repeat them.

15 Stability Study
676
Figure 15.30 Manual Creation of Inspection Lot for Storage Condition
Figure 15.31 Manual Creation of Inspection Lot for Stability Study
© 

677
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
Figure 15.32 Manual Inspection Lot with Inspection Type 1602
On successful creation of the manual inspection lot of inspection type 1602, use Trans-
action QA03 (or Transaction QA32) to display the same (see Figure 15.33). This screen
contains details about the newly created Inspection Lot 160000000007, as well as
details of the stability study, including physical sample 900000027, in the lower half of
the screen (not shown).
Figure 15.33 Display Manual Inspection Lot for Stability Study

sections.title: Change Storage Conditions
sections.text:
15.3.14 Change Storage Conditions
The next available option is to assess whether you can still make changes to storage
conditions after the release of physical samples and label printing.
In Action Box, choose Change Storage Conditions. At this stage, only a few details of the
physical samples are changeable, such as sample location, sample container, and sam-
ple quantity.
Select the line item for Stor.Cond. 00000001, and choose Save and Change Notifica-
tion.
If you don’t want to continue with a further stability study of a specific physical sample,
you can deactivate or block storage conditions at any time. In Action Box, choose Deac-
tivate Storage Conditions and then, on the Lock/Unlock Storage Condition screen,
select the checkmark under the Block Indicator column to lock or unlock storage condi-
tion(s). Finally, select the line item for Stor.Cond. 00000001, and choose Lock/Unlock
Change Notification.

sections.title: Change Stability Study Status
sections.text:
15.3.15 Change Stability Study Status
While performing all the steps, activities, and business processes in the stability study,
the system correspondingly continues to update its status. The stability study statuses
are available near the top of the screen (look for Notif. Status) on the main notification
screen.
Table 15.2 lists some of the statuses of the stability study.
Status Status Description Status Status Description
ACTV Stability Study Active SCDF Storage Condition Defined
CRIS Create Initial Sample STOR Stability Sample Stored
BOMA Bill of Material Assigned CRTS Create Testing Schedule
ISCR Initial Sample Created TSCR Testing Schedule Created
ISRL Initial Sample Released TSCO Testing Schedule Completed
CRIL Create Initial Test STRT Start of the Study
ILCR Initial Test Created COMP Study Completed
COIL Initial Test Completed CANC Study Canceled
DFSC Define Storage Condition INAC Study Inactive
Table 15.2 Selected Statuses of Stability Study

679
15.3 Stability Study for a Material
The following are some of the available options in a stability study:
 Deactivate Stability Study
You can also temporarily deactivate the stability study, if there is any such business
need. This may be the case when you want to temporarily put the entire stability
study project on hold.
In Action Box, choose Deactivate Stability Study. In the ensuing popup, which asks
you to confirm whether you want to deactivate the stability study, choose Yes to
confirm your decision. A deactivated stability study also deactivates the testing
schedule associated with the stability study.
 Activate Stability Study
Just like with deactivating, you can also reactivate an already deactivated stability
study. In Action Box, choose Activate Stability Study. In the ensuing popup, which
asks you to confirm whether you wish to activate the stability study, choose Yes to
confirm your decision. A reactivated stability study also activates the testing sched-
ule associated with the stability study.
 Cancel Stability Study
When there’s no further need to continue with a stability study, you can cancel it, if
needed. When you cancel a stability study, the system locks the testing schedule, as
well as the storage conditions of the sample(s). Further, you have to manually cancel
the inspection lots.
In Action Box, choose Cancel Stability Study, and in the ensuing popup, choose Yes
to confirm your decision. For this example, we chose No because we still want to
continue with the remaining steps of the stability study.
 Complete Stability Study
On completion of the stability study, it makes sense to update its status accordingly.
In Action Box, choose Complete Stability Study, and in the ensuing popup, confirm
your decision by choosing Yes. Note, however, that if there are any outstanding tests
or other open inspection lots, the system doesn’t allow their completion unless you
complete or cancel the inspection lots.
 Remove Stability Samples
On completion of the stability study, you can remove the samples of the stability
study from their storage conditions. In Action Box, choose Remove Stability Samples
to remove physical samples from storage conditions; even partial removal of physi-
cal samples is possible.
Select the first line item, and choose Save and Change Notification (see Figure 15.34).

15 Stability Study

sections.title: Display Stability Study
sections.text:
15.3.16 Display Stability Study
With this, the standard end-to-end business process of the stability study and the
options that it offers are complete. Now that you’ve learned how to set up a stability
study and its business processes, we’ll show you how the system displays the stability
study information in reports or workflows.
Display Object for Study
In Action Box, choose Display Objects for Study. This is now the very first item of the
Action Box. Here, you’ll find a comprehensive audit trail that covers just about all the
information that we presented in this chapter, as well as the sequence of activities that
we undertook for the stability study with a material (see Figure 15.35).
Tips and Tricks
You can also choose the Display document button, located near the top of the stability
study screen, to get a view of the stability study document flow. However, the details
aren’t as comprehensive as you’ll find in the Display Objects for Study option.

Figure 15.35 Complete Trail of the Stability Study
Display Stability Study History
In Action Box, choose Display Stability History. Here, you’ll find the details of all the
results of all the inspection lots that were created and for which results were recorded
during the course of the entire stability study. This includes, for example, results of the
initial test, the individual storage conditions in which the samples were kept, inspec-
tion lots created, and their recorded results (see Figure 15.36 and Figure 15.37).

sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.text:
15.4 Configuration Basics
It should be a comfort knowing that the challenging task of configuring a stability
study in SAP S/4HANA becomes easy based on all the knowledge and experience
you’ve gained while configuring various other areas of QM. The main areas in which
the stability study uses prior experience or knowledge are sample management,
inspection lot creation and completion, notification creation with the catalog profile,
and the information system, especially the info structure.
This section begins by covering the configuration options available for the stability
study. Wherever the information is previously covered, we’ll refer to the same without
repeating the information. This includes, for example, the option to define and assign
number ranges to a notification type, the catalog profile, and inspection lot creation
from the configuration perspectives. This section does, however, cover the PP section
of the bill of materials (BOM), as well as the PM portion of the testing schedule, with ref-
erence to the maintenance plan category.
© 

683
15.4 Configuration Basics
Let’s start with the configuration basics of the stability study. The basic data sets up the
initial conditions to keep the initial samples of the stability study and includes packag-
ing, sample management, and storage conditions.
Tips and Tricks
To save you the effort of defining all the parameters in any configuration object and
also lessen the chances of errors, we suggest that you copy from one of the standard
objects available and then make the desired changes to the newly created object. The
copy function is available in all configuration objects. Look for the Copy As option.

sections.title: Primary Packaging
sections.text:
15.4.1 Primary Packaging
Physical samples make use of primary packaging, not just during the initial sample but
also in all activities in which samples are used or maintained. To set up primary pack-
aging, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Stability Study  Basic Data 
Define Primary Packaging. On the screen that appears for maintenance of the primary
package for the stability study, create new entries as needed.

sections.title: Physical Sample Container
sections.text:
15.4.2 Physical Sample Container
Refer to the configuration of a physical sample container in Chapter 10, Section 10.5.3.
Create new entries as deemed necessary and save.

sections.title: Storage Conditions
sections.text:
15.4.3 Storage Conditions
The storage condition is the physical condition in which a sample is stored. During the
stability study, it’s important to identify the storage condition in which a sample is
placed. To set up a storage condition, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management 
Stability Study  Basic Data  Define Storage Conditions. On the screen that appears, you
can create new entries as deemed necessary and save.

sections.title: Storage Locations
sections.text:
15.4.4 Storage Locations
Refer to the configuration section of Chapter 10, Section 10.5.4, for defining storage
locations.

sections.title: Bill of Material Usage
sections.text:
15.4.5 Bill of Material Usage
A BOM usage during the stability study stipulates the controls of its usage for various
functions. For example, a BOM usage may only be for costing purposes, while another
usage may be for production. The controls are defined accordingly. To set up a BOM

15 Stability Study
684
usage, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Stability Study  Basic Data 
Define Bill of Material Usage.
BOM usage 8 is specifically available for the stability study. You’ll notice the various
columns for usage 8, such as costing, production, and sales are marked with the No
Entry indicator (the indicator is denoted by a - sign in all six columns).

sections.title: Samples for Stability Study
sections.text:
15.4.6 Samples for Stability Study
Refer to the relevant sections of Chapter 10 on sample management for the following
nodes in stability study configuration:
 Define physical sample type (see Section 10.5.2)
 Define number ranges (see Section 10.5.1)

sections.title: Testing Schedule Category
sections.text:
15.4.7 Testing Schedule Category
In the testing schedule for a stability study, the configuration that you need to define is
to call objects that the system should create on the date of the testing. Some of the call
objects are PM notifications, PM orders, and QM inspection lots. Because we’d like the
system to create a QM inspection lot on its due date, we’ll cover the desired settings in
this section accordingly. To set up the testing schedule for a stability study, follow
menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Stability Study  Testing Schedule for Sta-
bility Study  Define Testing Schedule Category.
Figure 15.38 Maintenance Plan for Scheduling Type
Figure 15.38 shows the initial screen to define details of the testing schedule. Notice
that the Maint. plan cat. (maintenance plan category) ST is configured for the stability
study and stipulates that the called object will be inspection lot creation. The Ref.
© 

685
15.4 Configuration Basics
object (reference object) 0190 stipulates that the basis for trigging inspection lot cre-
ation for the stability study will be the physical sample. To the extreme right of Figure
15.38, the number ranges are assigned. The number ranges can be both internal and
external. Create new entries as deemed necessary and save.

sections.title: Maintenance Strategy
sections.text:
15.4.8 Maintenance Strategy
Because we used maintenance strategy QSTABI in this chapter, we’ll cover its features
to enable you to correlate the configuration with business processes. A maintenance
strategy defines the frequency with which the system creates an inspection lot (the call
object) on its schedule dates. Further, it also enables the business process owner to
define the tolerance for early or late initiation or completion of specific inspection
tasks.
To set up the maintenance strategy for the stability study, use Transaction IP11 or fol-
low menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Stability Study  Stability Planning 
Strategy  Edit. You’ll see an initial screen to create or change a maintenance strategy.
Choose QSTABI, and either double-click the QSTABI field or choose Details. This leads to
the screen shown in Figure 15.39.
Figure 15.39 contains the strategy unit that stipulates the time unit of measure that the
system uses to create call objects. This unit of measure can be in hours, days, months,
or years.
Figure 15.39 Detailed Screen to Maintain Maintenance Strategy

15 Stability Study
686
A call horizon, defined as a percentage, enables the business process owner to control
when the system creates a call object on its planned or due date. For example, a 0% call
horizon means that as soon as the planned or due date of the call objects (in this case,
inspection lots) is reached, the system immediately creates the inspection lot. Simi-
larly, a 90% call horizon means that the system calls the object on a time horizon of
90% from the date of the next planned inspection lot creation. Other available options
are how the system should respond when there are deviations between planned and
actual tasks, such as inspection lot creation, its results recording, and its usage decision.
You can define not only the tolerance for early or late completion in percentages, but
also how much (as a percentage) the system should shift in dates when it finds devia-
tions between planned and actual tasks.
Choose Packages on the left side of Figure 15.40. This screen contains the cycle length,
in months, that the system uses to calculate the next time it creates a call object (for the
stability study, it’s an inspection lot) on its due date.
Figure 15.40 Maintenance Packages

sections.title: Notification Type
sections.text:
15.4.9 Notification Type
Because this chapter focuses on a stability study with a material, the corresponding QM
notification type in SAP is QS. To view details of the notification type for the stability
study, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Stability Study  Quality Noti-
fication for Stability Study  Open Stability Study  Define Notification Type. On the ini-
tial screen for various available notification types, choose Notification Type QS, which
leads to the detailed screen in Figure 15.41 for notification type QS. Notice that the
assigned catalog profile enables the availability of relevant tasks and activity codes to
notification type QS. It’s also important to note that the Update Group (stats) field is set
to 34, which updates the info structure for reporting purposes. We’ll cover info struc-
tures in Chapter 18.

sections.title: Action Box
sections.text:
15.4.11 Action Box
A highly important aspect of the stability study is to gain a comprehensive understand-
ing of the Action Box, which is available to facilitate the business process side. It facili-
tates the availability of all common business transactions in one place (in the stability
study notification), meaning the user is no longer required to navigate to different
screens and options. To navigate to Action Box for the stability study, follow menu path
SAP IMG  Quality Management  Stability Study  Quality Notification for Stability
Study  Perform Stability Study  Notification Functions  Define Action Box.
On the initial screen to configure Action Box, choose Define Functions for the Action
Box, and this leads to an overview of various notification types available in the system.
Choose Notification Type QS.
Here, the system automatically copies the catalog profile from Figure 15.41. You can add
the relevant codes for tasks and activities so that, subsequently, the same becomes
available on the notification screen of the stability study. Next, choose Activities in the
dialog structure to see the screen in Figure 15.42, which shows an overview of all the
activities that were visible in Action Box. Choose the first activity, Create Initial Sample,
and then choose Details. The screen that appears shows the detailed view of the Create
Initial Sample function. The important information to note is the assignment of the

15 Stability Study
688
function module to the creation of the initial sample. If a company has created a busi-
ness-specific function module to cater to a unique process, then the consultant or the
business process owner can assign it at this stage.
Choose Dependent Follow-Up Functions in Figure 15.42, and you can add a new function
for Dependent Follow-Up Function to the function or the Create Initial Sample action.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
15.5 Summary
In this chapter, we covered a series of logical and sequential steps that can be used to
cover just about all the business scenarios for implementing a stability study with a
material in QM. In addition to highlighting the importance of the QM master data
needed to implement a stability study, we also covered the cross-area integration of
QM with PP, PM, and MM. Various possible scenarios and their implications on the sta-
bility study were addressed.
We also covered the configuration steps needed to successfully implement a stability
study. A lot of information was drawn from previous experience of configuring and
implementing various subareas of QM, such as sample management, inspection lot
completion, and notification creation.
The next chapter covers the processes in failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) and
the control plan.
